author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Late in his theatrical career, Shakespeare wrote a play about a man arranging performances that other people experience as reality. The island makes the exercise of power visible as an act of staging.

hook.text: If you could punish everyone who hurt you, when would you stop?

paragraphs: Prospero has spent years on an island remembering a betrayal. When the people involved come within reach, he has unusual power to determine what they see, fear and believe.

That power turns the island into a theatre. Some characters are frightened into self-examination; others discover opportunities for schemes of their own. Prospero can manage an encounter, but managing someone is not the same as knowing what they will become.

The play's beauty sits beside uncomfortable claims of ownership. Ariel wants freedom. Caliban disputes the story by which his home has become another man's domain. Miranda meets the visitors with a curiosity her father's plans cannot entirely contain.

Read for the difference between bringing someone under control and making peace with them. If you could arrange a perfect reckoning with the people who wronged you, what would persuade you that the reckoning was complete?

orientation.text: Prospero's plans organise the action, but listen to Ariel's and Caliban's accounts of the island too. Their relationship to his authority differs sharply.
